art.title: Fair in Brittany
art.why: A busy market crowd with cattle under a church spire: the lively, ordinary world Chesterton loved against the closed circle of the maniac. No NGA painting of a fool or jester.

art.title: The Adoration of the Magi
art.why: Mary and the child sit before a rocky cave: the God in the cave. Chesterton's chapter treats both shepherds and Magi. Free Nativities (Lotto, Perino) show barns, not caves.

art.title: Buffalo Trail: The Impending Storm
art.why: A mountain landscape under towering storm clouds: Barth's thunderclap. American, not Swiss: say so (Calame's Swiss Landscape has no storm).

art.title: Old Factory
art.why: A brown factory with tall chimney beside a field: the factory work Weil took on in 1934-35. No workers shown.
No NGA Oxford scene or door that fits (searched oxford, college, door, doorway).

art.title: The Adoration of the Magi
art.why: A long line of travellers with horses and camels winds from a city to the child: the journey of the Magi. (Botticelli's Adoration is claimed by The world church.)

music.why: Rossetti's carol of the Almighty in a stable, Chesterton's paradox sung.
Mozart, whom Barth played every morning before work.
The Magi's journey in a Victorian carol, beside Eliot's harder version.

memory.title: A hard time we had of it
memory.ref: T. S. Eliot, 'Journey of the Magi' (1927), an excerpt: the closing lines from 'All this was a long time ago, I remember' to 'I should be glad of another death.' Verbatim from the 1927 Ariel edition.
